explanation: `high` is initialized to `arr.length` instead of `arr.length - 1`, but the loop uses the inclusive condition `low <= high`. When the target is greater than every element in the array, `low` keeps climbing toward `high` until they meet at `arr.length` itself — at that point `mid = (low + high) / 2` equals `arr.length`, and `arr[mid]` throws an out-of-bounds access. A correct version would either initialize `high = arr.length - 1` (keeping the inclusive condition) or keep `high = arr.length` but use the exclusive condition `low < high`.
prompt: Is this binary search safe for every target value, or can it misbehave?
